# Traccia — The Open-Source Agent Control Plane

AI agents can act. Traccia controls what they're allowed to do.

Traccia is a production-ready Python SDK for observing, evaluating, and enforcing policies on AI agents and LLM applications at runtime.

Built on OpenTelemetry, Traccia provides distributed tracing, token and cost tracking, evaluation, governance evidence, and runtime policy enforcement across AI agents, agentic workflows, and multi-agent systems.

Framework-agnostic and built for OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI, and LLM applications in production.

Traccia is available on PyPI.

## Features

### Runtime Control

- Runtime Policies : @govern can deny or reshape LLM or tool calls at runtime using policies such as Spend Cap, Model Boundary, and Loop Cap

- Guardrail Detection : Passive detection of AI safety controls, provider-native safeguards, and custom guardrails

- Security Controls : No secrets in logs and configurable data truncation

### Observability & Tracing

- Automatic Instrumentation : Auto-patch OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini (google-genai), Groq (groq), requests, and HTTP libraries

- Framework Integrations : Support for LangChain, CrewAI, and OpenAI Agents SDK

- LLM-Aware Tracing : Track tokens, costs, prompts, completions, and latency automatically

- OpenTelemetry Metrics : Emit OTEL-compliant metrics for accurate token and cost tracking independent of sampling

- Decorator-Based Tracing : Trace any function with the @observe decorator

- Multiple Exporters : OTLP-compatible export to Grafana Tempo, Jaeger, Zipkin, SigNoz, Console, or File

- Production-Ready Architecture : Rate limiting, error handling, configuration validation, and reliable flushing

- High Performance : Efficient batching, async support, and low-overhead instrumentation

### Evaluation & Development

- Offline Evaluation : evaluate() runs a task and scorers over a dataset and saves an experiment you can open, compare, and attach on promote

- Prompt Management : load_prompt / prefetch_prompts with cache, stale-while-revalidate, fallback, and traccia.prompt.* span identity

- Zero-Configuration Setup : Simple init() call with automatic configuration discovery

- Type-Safe Configuration : Full Pydantic validation and configuration management

### Governance & Compliance

- AI Governance and Compliance : EU AI Act and HIPAA-oriented evidence, transparency records, integrity verification, and PII/PHI redaction helpers

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Installation

pip install traccia

### Basic Usage

from traccia import init , observe # Initialize (auto-loads from traccia.toml if present) init () # Trace any function @ observe () def my_function ( x , y ): return x + y # That's it! Traces are automatically created and exported result = my_function ( 2 , 3 )

### With LLM Calls

from traccia import init , observe from openai import OpenAI init () # Auto-patches OpenAI client = OpenAI () @ observe ( as_type = "llm" ) def generate_text ( prompt : str ) -> str : response = client . chat . completions . create ( model = "gpt-4" , messages = [{ "role" : "user" , "content" : prompt }] ) return response . choices [ 0 ]. message . content # Automatically tracks: model, tokens, cost, prompt, completion, latency text = generate_text ( "Write a haiku about Python" )

### Gemini (google-genai)

from traccia import init from google import genai init () # Auto-patches google-genai client = genai . Client () response = client . interactions . create ( model = "models/gemini-flash-latest" , input = "Write a haiku about Python" , )

### Groq (groq)

from traccia import init from groq import Groq init () # Auto-patches groq (sync and async clients) client = Groq () response = client . chat . completions . create ( model = "llama-3.3-70b-versatile" , messages = [{ "role" : "user" , "content" : "Write a haiku about Python" }], ) # Streaming is traced too: the span stays open until the stream is read, closed, or dropped. for chunk in client . chat . completions . create ( model = "llama-3.3-70b-versatile" , messages = [{ "role" : "user" , "content" : "Write a haiku about Python" }], stream = True , ): print ( chunk . choices [ 0 ]. delta . content or "" , end = "" )

Each call gets an llm.groq.chat.completions span and goes through the Spend Cap. Settlement charges Groq's reported usage at Groq's own price (cached prompt tokens at the cached rate); a stream closed or failed partway is charged an estimate of what it produced; a stream dropped without close() has its request aborted and is charged its full reservation, as is a with_streaming_response call, whose body you read yourself. A call still open at stop_tracing() ends its span; when the Spend Cap reserved budget for it, it is also aborted and charged that reservation (unless Groq reported usage), and otherwise it is left running, so a stream another thread is reading keeps working. Groq reports usage only at the end of a stream, so a call without it records its estimated token counts on the span instead ( llm.usage.source is estimated ), the same counts an estimate is charged. with_raw_response works as before. Calls made to Groq through the OpenAI client ( base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1" ) go through the OpenAI integration instead, so use the groq client for Groq.

### Load a versioned prompt

Fetch prompts from your Traccia prompt registry by name and deploy label. Compiling fills {{variables}} and stamps the active span with prompt identity.

from traccia import init , observe , load_prompt , prefetch_prompts init ( api_key = "..." , prompt_cache_ttl_s = 60 ) prefetch_prompts ([ "support-reply" ]) # optional warm-up @ observe ( as_type = "llm" ) def reply ( question : str ) -> str : prompt = load_prompt ( "support-reply" , label = "production" , fallback = { "type" : "chat" , "messages" : [{ "role" : "system" , "content" : "You are a helpful assistant." }], }, ) messages = prompt . compile ( question = question ) # pass messages to your LLM client return messages [ - 1 ][ "content" ]

Requires the Traccia platform : create a workspace API key under Settings → API Keys . Tracing and prompt fetch use the same key and default to https://api.traccia.ai . Pass an explicit fallback so agents can still run if a fetch fails. See Prompts in the SDK .

### Run an experiment

evaluate() runs a task and scorers over a dataset. By default the run is saved as an experiment you can open in the app under Evaluate → Experiments , compare against other runs, and attach when you promote a prompt. Use the same workspace API key as tracing and load_prompt .

from traccia import init , evaluate , load_prompt init ( api_key = "..." ) prompt = load_prompt ( "support-reply" , label = "production" ) def task ( inp ): messages = prompt . compile ( ** inp ) return call_model ( messages ) result = evaluate ( "support-reply-v3" , data = "support-golden" , # platform dataset name or UUID task = task , scorers = [ "exact_match" ], # builtins, platform names/ids, or callables prompt = "support-reply" , # labels the experiment cell with this prompt ) print ( result . summary ()) print ( result . url )

- Persist is on by default. Set persist=False for a local-only loop (no experiment URL).

- Inline rows work as [{"input": {...}, "expected": "..."}] . With persist on, Traccia still saves a full experiment (helper datasets named sdk-eval/... are hidden on Evaluate → Datasets unless you turn on Show SDK-Created ).

- Builtins run in-process: exact_match , contains , json_valid . Mix in platform scorers (LLM-as-judge, Jev Decision, code) by name or UUID. Pass provider_keys= for judges ( typesafe for Jev). A Jev score keeps each question on the experiment.

- One throwing row does not abort the run. That cell records error ; other items still score. Configuration and API failures raise EvaluateError .

- If the first task argument is named row , item , example , or case , Python passes the full row. Any other name (including input ) receives only the input dict.

See Evaluate in the SDK and the walkthrough Run Experiments From Code .

### Run evals in CI

traccia eval runs a task script, saves an experiment, and writes summary.json . The process exit code is the gate: 0 pass, 1 quality miss, 2 bad command or baseline, 3 untrustworthy evidence, 4 the experiment did not save, 5 the summary file was not written. With no pass-rate bar, a green check is Execution Only . Add --min-pass-rate or --max-drop for a Quality Gate . --max-drop 0.05 is five percentage points. --max-task-cost-increase 0.2 is 20 percent.

The script defines task and, for a function in the file, a scorers dict passed as --scorer local:name . A local scorer cannot pass --max-drop . Pass --prompt with --prompt-version or --prompt-label when the experiment should record a prompt version. Platform LLM-judge and Jev scorers read OPENAI_API_KEY , ANTHROPIC_API_KEY , GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY , GROQ_API_KEY , and TYPESAFE_API_KEY , or a JSON object in TRACCIA_PROVIDER_KEYS . Those values are not written into the summary. Each Jev question is gated on its own pass rate. Execution Only means no pass-rate gate; cost and latency gates can still apply.

traccia eval experiments/support_agent.py \ --output summary.json \ --dataset support-golden \ --scorer exact_match \ --min-pass-rate 0.9 \ --baseline-prompt support-reply \ --max-drop 0.05

See Run Evals In CI .

# Telegram AI Bot Pro

A private TypeScript Telegram assistant with text and voice conversations, photo analysis and editing, image generation, web search with sources, document questions, projects, named conversations, explicit saved memory, usage controls, streaming replies and durable background jobs. MIT licensed.

“Pro” names this repository's feature set. It does not grant a ChatGPT subscription or provider account access.

## Get started

Requirements: Node.js 26.13+ within Node 26 , npm 11, a Telegram bot token, an OpenAI project API key with billing and model access. Outgoing voice messages require FFmpeg with libopus ; the Docker image includes it. Incoming voice transcription needs no FFmpeg.

nvm use npm ci cp .env.example .env # Fill in required settings before starting. npm run dev

Required settings:

- TELEGRAM_API_KEY : token from @BotFather .

- OPENAI_API_KEY : private OpenAI project key.

- ALLOWED_TELEGRAM_USER_IDS : comma-separated numeric IDs. Only these users in private chats are processed.

Default chat model: gpt-6.1-sol . Override it with OPENAI_CHAT_MODEL using a Responses model supporting vision, document inputs, web_search and image_generation . Missing or blank values use the default.

Default image model: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst , quality high . Default outgoing speech model: gpt-realtime-2.1-mini , voice marin . Model availability must be checked against your own account. Configuration does not establish provider acceptance.

For FFmpeg on macOS, install with brew install ffmpeg ; on Debian/Ubuntu, install the ffmpeg package. Check that your build supports the libopus encoder. FFMPEG_PATH can point to a trusted executable.

npm run build npm start

## Commands

Voice replies start off . Every outgoing voice message is labelled AI-generated voice . Text answers remain available even if narration fails. Long answers are not silently truncated for speech: use /speak with a shorter passage.

Natural-language requests can invoke image generation or web search automatically. Explicit commands provide a predictable way to request them. remember: … and forget … manage saved notes without a model call. The bot never extracts long-term notes automatically from ordinary conversation.

## Photos and documents

Send a photo or original JPEG/PNG/static WebP file, with optional instructions in its caption. Continue asking questions about it. /image , /edit and /search also work in captions. Reply to an older photo or document to attach that exact source to the current request. Generated images arrive as original PNG documents.

Supported document extensions: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, TXT, MD, CSV, JSON . Send a document with a question, or without a caption for a summary. Follow-up questions reuse retained files. PDFs and Office files are parsed by OpenAI; text documents must be UTF-8. Signatures catch obvious PDF/Office/image mismatches; complete file validity and provider parsing are checked downstream. Embedded pictures/layout in non-PDF documents are not guaranteed to be available to the model. Convert to PDF when visual layout matters.

Reference albums collect up to ten updates during a 750 ms window and share one download deadline. Items arriving later receive the usual busy response if processing has begun. Send files separately and wait for each reply when predictable batch membership matters.

Examples:

[photo] Read this sign and translate it into English. /image A realistic cat portrait in a spacesuit, square composition [reply to that image] /edit Replace the background with a beach [PDF] Summarize the obligations and point to the relevant pages. [follow-up] What does section 4 say? /search What changed in the latest Node.js release? /new Work /remember Answer concisely in English. /voice auto

## Data and limits

Production state is saved to STATE_DB_PATH (default ./data/bot.sqlite ). Text history, images, documents, conversation names, saved notes and voice preferences are private local data. Keep this file out of source control and use a persistent Docker volume. :memory: selects disposable state. Tests inject isolated stores and do not open your production database.

Saved conversation names, notes and voice settings survive restarts. Retained message history and attachments also survive restarts within TTL and capacity limits . History defaults to one hour of inactivity and 20 complete turns per conversation. Expired histories are pruned at startup and on subsequent conversation access; names and explicit notes are retained separately. /reset preserves other conversations and saved notes. /forget removes saved notes but cannot erase earlier text containing the same information; clear affected conversations too when needed.

Foreground updates are serialized per user. A background job locks its conversation; foreground work in another conversation can proceed within the global concurrency cap. /stop remains available during foreground work. Overlapping foreground updates receive a busy response. Provider failures do not commit partial turns. Successful complete-turn writes and capacity evictions are transactional in SQLite. Text and media have bounded request/history budgets. Daily quotas and configurable estimated-spend reservations apply separately; see the Pro workspace commands below. Estimates are not provider invoices or a hard billing cap.

Text, audio, attached files, saved notes and relevant history are sent to OpenAI for requested processing. Search may send generated queries to search providers. Responses use store: false ; this does not establish zero retention by OpenAI or Telegram. Requests and raw provider exceptions are not logged. The SQLite file is access-restricted but is not encrypted at rest by this application.

## Pro workspaces and controls

Daily accounting uses UTC regardless of schedule timezone. Defaults allow 100 paid operations and $10 of configured cost estimates per owner/day. Tool calls and speech have separate limits. Failures and cancelled attempts retain their reservations because provider charges may already have occurred. Configure provider-side spending controls too. /erase retains minimal current-day quota counters to prevent limit bypass.

Projects and jobs retain files independently of conversation TTL. PDF export embeds a bundled font for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic text with limited punctuation; unsupported characters produce a clear error directing you to Markdown/JSON. No cloud PDF conversion is used. See the user guide for full syntax and lifecycle rules.

## Development and tests

npm run check # types, lint, formatting, unit tests and production compilation npm run test:unit # unit tests only; npm test is equivalent npm run test:coverage # require 100% executable src lines, branches and functions

Tests live beside their implementation in __tests__ ; shared in-memory doubles live in src/__tests__/helpers.ts . Production compilation excludes every __tests__ directory. Only test files are excluded from coverage; production code has no coverage-ignore annotations.

Only unit tests are authorized and maintained. HTTP/WebSocket transports, SQLite/filesystem access, process lifecycle, FFmpeg spawning and PDF rendering use controlled doubles. Tests do not call live services, open databases, run application subprocesses, invoke FFmpeg, build Docker or render browsers. They require no API keys and incur no API charges. Node's experimental module-mocking flag is included in test scripts.

CI runs static checks, unit tests, the 100% coverage gate and a dependency advisory query ( npm audit , network metadata only). It does not install FFmpeg or build Docker. Unit coverage establishes exercised local control flow; live model access, native SQLite durability, PDF layout, audio fidelity and deployment behavior remain unqualified. npm is the sole package manager; commit lockfile changes with dependencies.
